Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

	at org.apache.commons.jxpath.JXPathTestCase.assertXPathValueIterator(JXPathTestCase.java:158)

Title: Diagnosis of test `testNodeSetReturn`
Details: The test `testNodeSetReturn` in the class `ExtensionFunctionTest` fails when asserting that the XPath evaluation of the expression `test:nodeSet()` returns a sequence of bean objects. The expected result is a list containing the actual bean objects (`[Nested: Name 1, Nested: Name 2]`), but the actual result is a list of paths or pointers (`[[/beans[1], /beans[2]]]`). This indicates that instead of returning the actual nodes or objects, the XPath evaluation returned their address-like representations or pointers.

The failure points to a discrepancy in how the function `test:nodeSet()` is implemented or how it computes its return value. The class `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.ExtensionFunction` and its methods `.compute(org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.EvalContext)` and `.computeValue(org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.EvalContext)` are potentially involved in the evaluation and computation of extension functions like `test:nodeSet`.

The bug may have occurred because the `ExtensionFunction.compute` or `computeValue` method returns the node pointers or path representations instead of the nodes themselves when the function `nodeSet()` is called. The test expects the actual node objects, not their pointers. This mismatch yields the assertion error in `assertXPathValueIterator`.

To confirm this diagnosis, we need to examine the implementation of `ExtensionFunction.compute` and `ExtensionFunction.computeValue` to see how they handle the return values of extension functions, particularly focusing on the type checks or conversions from pointers to node values.

Next step: Retrieve the source code of `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.ExtensionFunction.computeValue(org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.EvalContext)` to see how the return value is computed and possibly converted.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
